frontier.hypothesis: Target's missing `addu $t3,$v0,$zero` preheader copy appears when the loop bound's load result stays live past the rotation guard — i.e. the guard consumes one pseudo and the loop-carried bound is a genuinely separate pseudo that copy propagation cannot fold.
frontier.mechanism: In our form the load destination IS the loop-bound pseudo, so GCC emits `lw $t3` and branches on $t3 directly. In target the load lands in $v0, blez reads $v0, and the preheader copies $v0 into $t3 — two pseudos surviving into RA. A C-level duplicate (`var_v0 = D_800A38C8; var_t3 = var_v0;`) is folded by copy propagation (KILLED this session), so the second pseudo has to be created by a pass, not by the source: the candidates are LICM hoisting a load whose value the rotation guard also needs, and loop.c's own bound-copy in the preheader.
frontier.next_probe: Spell the bound as a memory expression read by the loop test itself — `while (var_t1 < D_800A38C8)` — with no count local at all, and read both instruments (tmp/grind/func_80037B00/s6/frame_probe.sh for vars, sandbox --disable all for the score) plus the .loop and .combine dumps in tmp/grind/func_80037B00/dumps/. If LICM hoists the load into the preheader while the rotation guard keeps its own copy, the `addu` appears and build_insns should reach 36. If instead a second `lw` appears, read the .loop dump to see whether loop.c created a bound copy at all in this shape, and pivot to making the bound's first use be something other than the guard.

frontier.hypothesis: The `lui/addiu` for D_80102810 moves from stream position 1-2 to target's 6-7 when the base-pointer initialisation is loop-invariant code that LICM places in the preheader, rather than a straight-line statement written before the loop.
frontier.mechanism: Target emits the `la` after the blez, i.e. inside the guarded preheader — the classic position for an invariant hoisted OUT of the loop body. Our form assigns `var_a3` before the while, so it is ordinary straight-line code above the guard and sched1 pulls it further up to cover the lw's load delay. Deleting the programmer's pre-guard is what created the orphan (do not re-add it — KILLED this session), so the placement has to come from LICM instead of from dominance.
frontier.next_probe: Move the base-pointer initialisation INTO the loop body as a genuine loop-invariant expression the algorithm justifies — e.g. carry only the byte offset in the loop and write `var_a1 = (s8 *)&D_80102810 + off;` inside, letting LICM hoist the `la` into the preheader while the `addu` stays. Watch build_insns for an added per-iteration add; if it appears, try instead making `var_a3` the induction variable but initialising it from an expression that is only computed once the loop is known non-empty. Measure vars= at every step — the frame must survive.

frontier.hypothesis: The last register 2-swap (our counter=$t0/end=$t1 vs target's counter=$t1/end=$t0) closes by raising the end-pointer allocno's priority above the counter's, which the validated priority model says needs the end pointer's live_length shortened to 5-6 insns (pri 0.33-0.40) so it sorts between the base pointer (0.417) and the counter (0.286).
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare: pri = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/live_length, ties to lower pseudo number. The model reproduced this function's rank order exactly, so it is a forward oracle: adding a fourth ref to the end pointer overshoots (2*4/11 = 0.727, jumping above the base pointer and breaking a correct assignment), while shortening its live range from 11 to 5 or 6 lands it exactly in the gap. Birth order is the tiebreak if priorities collide.
frontier.next_probe: Re-derive the priority table for the s6 form first (rerun pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80037B00 with the candidate applied and read .flow/.greg — the numbers below are from the s0..s5 form and the ranks have shifted). Then look for a spelling that shortens the end pointer's live range without adding instructions: computing `var_t0` later in the block, or expressing the inner bound so the end pointer's first reference sits closer to its last. Check each candidate against the model on paper before compiling, and confirm with the .greg rank line rather than the score.
